notes: **2026-09-02** — (branch `fix/F11-run-cancel-skip-v2`, off master `c60fe214`; no schema change, no migration) — **F11 RUN CANCEL / SKIP RECONCILIATION (B129 Critical/B211/B146/B34).** Every cancelled run, and every run completed with a skipped stop, left its undelivered orders pinned to a stale `routeRunStopId` — invisible to the dispatch sweep and the trip builder (both require the pointer null), while the buyer card kept showing a driver and "you're next" for a called-off run. New private `routes.service.ts#releaseUndeliveredOrders(tx, stopIds)` (OUT_FOR_DELIVERY→CONFIRMED revert, then null both pointers for orders ∉ {DELIVERED, CANCELLED}) now runs inside the SAME transaction as both terminal writes: `updateRunStatus`'s CANCELLED/COMPLETED branch (in-tx read of the run's non-COMPLETED stop ids) and one line after the RF-016 auto-complete's `tx.routeRun.update` in both `completeStop` and `completeWithPayment`. SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS — including un-cancel — stays the bare update: un-cancel re-pins nothing and is not a path back to the released orders, since `createRun` refuses a route that already carries a SCHEDULED/IN_PROGRESS run - re-dispatch means cancelling again, then dispatching a fresh run. Every release call site logs its released count. `reopenStop` refuses `stop SKIPPED ∧ run COMPLETED` (the new state pair the release makes reachable) with a 400, decided before ownership and before any transaction; the REFUSAL is that state pair alone but the MESSAGE branches on whether the stop still holds orders, so a pre-deploy stranded row is pointed at the D4 repair instead of a trip builder that cannot see it. `findOneRun`'s legacy no-linked-orders fallback is skipped for any TERMINAL run - CANCELLED or COMPLETED (a run completed with every stop skipped releases its orders exactly like a cancel; without the guard the detail page shows those customers' CURRENT open orders as the run's contents). `orders.service.ts#getOrderTracking` returns `tracking: null` for a CANCELLED run's stop (checked right after the existing no-stop short-circuit); a SKIPPED own-stop keeps the full payload. **Sweep extraction (build-plan WP1(g)) was proposed and DROPPED by the lead** — `createRun`'s sweep stays byte-for-byte untouched (un-cancel is status-only, so it never gained a second caller). Mobile: `lib/skip-stop.ts#createSkipStopHandler` (pure; runId guard, in-flight guard, mutate-then-navigate, offline-queued counts as accepted) wired into the driver stop screen's Skip confirm via `useUpdateStopStatus` — before F11 that confirm was a bare `router.replace`, so Skip never sent a PATCH and the stop stayed PENDING (the `confirm-navigate` scan-ignore suppression covering exactly this is removed). `lib/order-tracking-logic.ts` gained `trackingHeadline` (cancelled > SKIPPED own-stop > IN_PROGRESS live-run copy > null) driving the buyer order screen's tracking line, and `trackingRefetchInterval` (now also polls while the run is IN_PROGRESS, not only while the order is OUT_FOR_DELIVERY/PARTIALLY_DELIVERED, so a CONFIRMED order can observe its own skip). Both mobile and web `useUpdate{RunStatus,RouteRunStatus}.onSuccess` refresh the order lists after a terminal write — mobile through the now-exported `lib/api/orders.ts#invalidateOrderCaches`, since the operator route-run screen that issues the cancel reads the `["admin","orders"]` family a bare `["orders"]` invalidation misses; web has one family and also adds `["trips-eligible-orders"]` (the trip-builder picker list) and `["trip-eligibility"]`. D4 historical repair for pre-fix stranded rows: `scripts/repair-f11-stranded-orders.mjs` (dry-run by default, derived scope query, JSONL before-state, `REPAIR-RUNBOOK.md` §2). Specs: `routes.service.run-terminal-release{,.pins}.spec.ts`, `orders.service.tracking-contract{,.pins}.spec.ts`, mobile `__tests__/{order-tracking-logic,skip-stop,f11-run-cancel-skip.pins}.test.ts`. Lesson **L-045** (a pointer that gates re-entry must be released by every transition that makes the pointed-at thing terminal, inside that transition's own tx, on the durable forward-path marker — never a side row a payment-only path skips). Follow-ups filed (not F11's, allocate B212+): `RouteRunStop.skipReason` has zero writers/readers repo-wide; `updateStopStatus` stays non-transactional with an unvalidated inline body; only `completeWithPayment` writes `deliveredQty`; no run-row `FOR UPDATE`, whose lock order is also inverted against `completeStop`/`completeWithPayment` (a concurrent operator cancel and driver stop completion can deadlock); un-cancel leaves a run that can be neither refilled nor re-dispatched until it is cancelled again; `deleteRun`/B209 + cancel-while-unsettled policy. || History in CHANGELOG.md (this directory).
